title: session-view v1
description: The read model's answer about the whole Horde, as core/projection produces it (step 2.2) and 'horde status --json' will print it (step 2.3). One session per sessionId any store knows, and for each one answer for every field in core/ownership.json's required, over every owner. Every answer is in core/tristate's form: a state (known, absent or unknown) and a reason; a known answer carries its value, typed per field - for a field the engine stores, exactly the value schema of schema/session-record.v1, which test/test-projection.ps1 compares. source names the store and field the answer was read from, by core/ownership.json's store ids; observedAt is when the source says the value was true; provisional is the ownership table's provisional mark for that field; shadow is what a shadow-only store (the layout saves) said without being trusted. A field the table drops is present and always unknown, its reason naming the drop. handles lists every live host handle, including handles no session answers, so a pane-first command's parity is read from this output; faults are the cardinality checks, one per kind, each known true with what was found, known false, or unknown with the reason; complete gives each store's completeness. WHAT THIS SCHEMA CANNOT SAY, because core/Schema.ps1 implements no oneOf, anyOf, if/then or dependencies: that value is present exactly when state is known, that reason is non-blank when state is unknown, and that a fault's found list is empty unless its answer is known true. Those rules are checked by Test-HordeSessionViewRules in core/Projection.ps1, and the schema is not weakened to pretend otherwise.
